chapter_title: The Chapter of the Elements that wept
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation: The Four Griefs of the External Truths

---

**¶2:**
The external truths — those truths proceeding from the Divine Good — underwent deep spiritual anguish three times. Then they were stilled. There remains a fourth anguish, for they will grieve at the final consummation. And then their mourning can cease, and never again will they suffer grief from that time onward.

---

**¶3:**
The first anguish was when they perceived falsity from evil — the opposing power about to erupt against them. They comprehended all that would befall them in their descent into the natural degree. They were aware of the evil that would rise and assail them, yet by Divine necessity they advanced toward it and contended with it. They prevailed over it; they held it fast. They bound it with their own external forms and their own faculties of action; they overcame its spiritual death, its self-love, and its falsity.

---

**¶4:**
[GAP-1] The second anguish was [when] the Divine Good — the celestial principle from which they proceeded — [ascend]ed out of the [GAP-2] deepest states of falsity and evil, and withdrew from them; that is the time when the Divine Good separated [GAP-3] these external truths from itself and left them in the lower degree. Indeed, when they perceived how the Divine Good had risen out of the deepest falsity and withdrawn from them, and that they were left behind amid the hostility of evil, they grieved and were afflicted in their inmost will. Yet what could they do, resigning [GAP-4] their will to every suffering. They [remained] behind and grew weakened under the weight of the oppressive burden of all labors of spiritual combat, until the time of consummation.

---

**¶5:**
[GAP-5] The third anguish was when the Divine Truth in its active proceeding separated the three degrees of operative external truths, placing them as the foundation beneath all things. The Divine Truth gave them an influx of perception to elevate their understanding and ascend toward interior states from that condition — and to pass through all the natural degrees of the mind until they should reach the state of celestial peace and rest, the heavenly state prepared for them. But when they perceived that the Divine Truth had withdrawn from them, while they themselves remained behind and had not yet ascended, at that moment the three degrees of operative external truths grieved. After their grief, they turned their will toward all the interior and elevated states that had been concealed from them, and they came into unanimity of purpose. For [GAP-6] they were to rise and attain the interior states, and pass beyond all natural conditions until the appointed time ordained for them all [GAP-7] at the consummation of all spiritual ages.

---

**¶6:**
The fourth anguish will come when the complete Divine Human form is taken up on the final day, and the external truths will grieve [GAP-8] over the interior life of those who lived in falsity and profanation — for they must yield [GAP-9] because their very faculties have been severed [GAP-10] by falsity from evil. And also those interior affections themselves — when the Divine Human form ascends and they are left behind — they will grieve in that they will remain in affliction forever. For they will be cut off and separated from the complete Divine Human form. And it is a necessity of Divine order that those interior affections which are given over to destruction receive retribution for the deeds they have done. They descend into the state of utter falsity and are bound with falsity from evil — just as they desired it and loved it, and placed their inmost love within it. At that very moment, when the complete Divine Human form rises up, they will grieve. And then they will cry out in anguish because they will be severed from the communion of this great Divine Human form. And they remain behind forever. This great anguish [GAP-11] is terrible; it occurs before the interior affections and [GAP-12] those who are given over to destruction in accordance with their works. And they [GAP-13] will grieve with that grief and never be silent, because they will not attain rest from that time onward.

---

**¶7:**
And so these too are the external truths belonging to the fundamental spiritual substances. This fourth anguish is the most wrenching for them. It is far worse than the three preceding griefs. This fourth time, the grief is not for themselves. Rather, they grieve and are afflicted in their will on behalf of those interior affections that will be cut off from peace — because rest will never come about for them, to grant them relief from torment forever.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: The garments, the sons of the First Man, wept bitterly three times. Then they were silent. There is a fourth time of weeping, for they will weep at the end. And then their crying can stop, and they will never again weep from this time on.

Now, the first time of their weeping is when they had seen the Darkness, the enemy being about to burst out against them. They understood everything that would happen to them. They were aware of the one that would rise and come upon them, but by necessity they hastened to him and fought with him. They mastered him, they detained him. They bound him with their body and their limbs, they overcame his death and his fire and his Darkness.

[The] second time that they wept is [when the]ir father, the First Man, [ascend]ed from the [abyss] of Darkness and left them behind; that is the time when he stripped [them off] and left them below. Indeed, when th[ey] s[aw] how the First Man had risen out of the abyss and [l]eft them behind, and that they were abandoned in the enmit[y, th]ey wept and were sore of heart. Still, what could they do, wishing [to rise up after him, yet they were unable. They gave] their heart to every affliction. They [remained b]ehind and grew [s]ick under the pressure of the weighty burden of all the works, until the end time.

[The] third time that they wept is when the Living Spirit stripped off the three garments of activity, placing them beneath all things. He gave them a sign to lift their heads and rise to the heights from that place; and to pass and journey through all the earths until they should reach the land of tranquilli[t]y and peace, the place of rest prepared for them. So, when they had seen him, that he had separated himself from them, while they themselves remained behind after him and had not ascended; at that moment when they stayed behind these three garments wept. After their crying, they turned their [hear]t to all the heights that were concealed from them, and were of one mind. For [they would] soar up and come to the heights; and pass over all things until the time that was ordained for them all [should come] at the end of the worlds.

[The f]ourth time when they will weep is when the [S]tatue will be taken up on the last day, and they will weep [for] the souls of the liars and blasphemers; for they may give [them up] because their limbs have been severed [by the power] of the Darkness. And also [th]ose souls, when the Statue will go up and they are left alo[n]e, they will weep in that they will rema[in] behind in affliction for ever. For they wi[ll be cut off] and separated from the Last Statue. An[d it is] a necessity to take these souls who are ready for loss as retribution for the deeds that they have done. They go i[n to] this [darkne]ss and are bound with the Darkness; just as they desired it and loved it, and placed their treasure with it. At that very moment, when the Last Statue rises up, the[y wi]ll weep. And then they will scream out loud because they will be severed from the company of this great Statue. And they remain behind for ever. This great weeping [and lamentation] is terrible, it occurs in front of the souls and [those] who are ready for loss in accordance with their deeds. And they [will] weep with that crying, they will never be silent; because they will not attain rest from this time on.

So, they too are the garments of these elements. This fourth time of weeping is heart-rending for them. It is much worse for them than these other three times of weeping before. This fourth time the weeping is not for themselves. Rather they weep and are heartsore for these soul[s] who will be cut off from peace, because rest will not come about for them, to allow them to rest from torment for ever.

fills.explanation: The pattern of each weeping section ("The second time," "The third time") requires the definite article, consistent with the parallel structure throughout the chapter.

The spiritual reading gives "deepest states of falsity and evil," and the same paragraph later says "risen out of the abyss," confirming the editor's choice of "abyss" as the natural-plane term for the deepest region of Darkness.

The spiritual reading says the Divine Good "separated these external truths from itself"; in the Kephalaia's garment imagery, the First Man "stripped them off" — removing his garments/armor — which is the standard Manichaean expression for this separation.

fills.explanation: The garments wished to ascend after the First Man but could not; the spiritual reading's "resigning their will" requires a verb of surrender ("gave") before "their heart to every affliction," and the narrative of being left behind strongly constrains the content of the wish (to rise after him) and the outcome (inability, then resignation).
Parallel structure with ¶4 ("The second time") requires "The third time that they wept," and the spiritual reading confirms "The third anguish."

The spiritual reading says "they were to rise and attain the interior states," expressing determined future intention; "they would soar up" conveys this purposive resolution in the Kephalaia's register.

The clause "until the time that was ordained for them all [GAP-7] at the end of the worlds" requires a verbal element; "should come" completes the temporal construction naturally, meaning the appointed time arrives at the consummation.

The spiritual reading says the external truths "will grieve over the interior life of those who lived in falsity"; "weep for the souls" is the natural-plane expression of this grieving on behalf of others, consistent with ¶7's confirmation that the fourth weeping is not for themselves.

The spiritual reading says "they must yield" — in the Kephalaia's register, the garments must "give them up" (surrender the lost souls) because the light-limbs trapped in those souls have been severed by Darkness.

The spiritual reading says "severed by falsity from evil"; in the Kephalaia's natural register, "by the power of the Darkness" is the standard instrumental phrase describing the agency of evil, and occurs frequently throughout the corpus.
Doublets are characteristic of Kephalaia style; "weeping and lamentation" is a natural paired expression in this register, intensifying the description of the fourth and most terrible grief.

The spiritual reading places "those who are given over to destruction" at this position; "those" serves as the demonstrative introducing the second group — "the souls and those who are ready for loss" — paralleling the structure of the passage.

The entire ¶6 describes the fourth weeping in future/eschatological tense ("they will weep," "they will scream"), and the spiritual reading confirms "they will grieve with that grief"; the future marker "will" is required.
